ai.title: Initial @codebuff/sdk v0.0.1 package setup and publishing scripts
ai.summary: New `@codebuff/sdk` package added with `CodebuffClient` and `runNewChat` for programmatic agent interaction. Includes `scripts/publish.js` to transform workspace deps into peer deps and prepare `dist/` for npm. Configured `tsconfig.json` for standalone compilation with declaration maps. Requires global `codebuff` CLI and `CODEBUFF_API_KEY`.

eli5.text: A new toolkit for developers called the Codebuff SDK is now available, letting them write programs that can automatically run AI coding agents to edit code, start new conversations, and read responses as they happen. The publishing process has been set up so the toolkit can be downloaded from the standard package directory, with scripts that convert internal dependencies into ones it expects to find already installed on the developer's machine, and the package is public under a permissive license. Today, anyone can install it, provided they have the matching command-line tool and an access key already in place.

ai.title: SDK v0.0.2 replaces workspace dep with zod
ai.summary: Bumps @codebuff/sdk to v0.0.2. Drops @codebuff/common workspace dependency for zod ^3.23.8. Switches imports to relative paths ../../common/src/... in client.ts, process-stream.ts, and types.ts. Publish script updates main/types/exports to ./sdk/src/index.js/.d.ts. processStream refactored to return new Promise directly.

eli5.text: The SDK package that developers use to connect to Codebuff switched from using Codebuff's own internal tool library to a widely-used third-party validation library called zod. If you're a developer building on top of Codebuff's SDK, your project no longer needs to include Codebuff's internal common package as a dependency, instead it now relies on zod, which many JavaScript projects already use. The publishing setup was also adjusted so the package points to its actual source files when distributed, and one background streaming function was rewritten to be more straightforward. This is now live in SDK version 0.0.2.

ai.summary: Bumps @codebuff/sdk version to 0.0.3. Modifies sdk/scripts/publish.js to replace wildcard file patterns (*.js, *.d.ts) with explicit directory entries (sdk/, common/) in the package.json files field. This ensures all built artifacts from the sdk and common subdirectories are correctly included in the published package. Scope limited to sdk/package.json and sdk/scripts/publish.js.

eli5.text: The toolkit that other apps use to connect to CodeBuff now ships with a more reliable list of the built files it includes, so any developer importing it gets the complete set of helper files from both the main toolkit folder and its shared utilities folder instead of a smaller wildcard-based selection. This only affects the developers who pull the toolkit into their own projects; you do not see a difference unless you are building on top of it. The change is part of the toolkit update that is available now.

ai.title: Reduce PROFITMARGIN to 5.5% in message-cost-tracker
ai.summary: PROFIT_MARGIN constant lowered from 0.3 to 0.055 in backend/src/llm-apis/message-cost-tracker.ts. Adjusts internal cost calculation logic to reflect a tighter margin.

eli5.text: The company has quietly lowered its built-in profit cushion when calculating what it costs to use its AI-powered coding assistant, dropping the markup it applies to the underlying AI model fees from 30% down to 5.5%. This means internal cost estimates, the numbers developers and finance teams rely on to understand how much each AI request actually costs the company, are now much closer to the raw price of the AI services themselves, rather than inflating them by a larger margin. If you look at the behind-the-scenes cost-tracking system, you’d see the same expenses reported with a tighter margin, but this is an internal adjustment that doesn’ change what you pay or how the assistant works.

ai.title: Unescape newlines in .agents prompts
ai.summary: Added `scripts/convert-escaped-newlines.ts` to unescape `\n` sequences in `.agents` prompt files. This fixes rendering issues in `ask.ts`, `base*.ts`, `file-picker.ts`, and `knowledge-keeper.ts` where system prompts were stored as single-line strings with escaped newlines. The change ensures prompts are formatted correctly for agent execution.

eli5.text: The coding assistant's instructions were stored as one long line of text with \n characters instead of real line breaks, causing the prompts to render as a single run-on paragraph. A new conversion step now properly formats these instructions so they display correctly with line breaks, headers, and spacing as intended. You would have seen the assistant's behavior guide as one unbroken block of text instead of the readable, structured document it was meant to be.

ai.title: Add open-source model agent suite
ai.summary: New agent configs in `.agents/opensource/` define a base orchestrator and specialized subagents (coder, file-picker, researcher, reviewer) using only open-source models like `qwen3-coder` and `gpt-oss-120b`. This provides a free, local-capable alternative to proprietary backends. Changes affect core agent definitions and model utility constants.

eli5.text: A coding assistant you can run entirely for free on your own computer now exists. The change adds a new team of specialized helpers, each with a clear job: one writes code, another finds the right files to edit, a third researches questions online, and one reviews work for mistakes. The main helper coordinates them, just like before, but everything talks only to free, publicly available models instead of paid ones, so nothing in the tool uses a paid service anymore.

The list itself still contains the same actions, just written on fewer lines. If you looked at the files today, you would see the list sitting where the build process now saves it, instead of where it used to be written and then ignored.

eli5.text: Agents now receive the actual answer from a tool directly, instead of a box that just points to the answer. When an agent asks another agent to build something, that builder can use the answer right away without opening an extra container first. This also means agents no longer need to check whether a step should stop on its own. The change is live today across the built-in agents, so any workflow that spawns or inspects tool usage will behave differently.

eli5.text: The internal helper that finds relevant files for you now gives shorter, more to-the-point answers instead of brief ones. You won't see this file directly, but if you ever get a suggested list of files back, the summaries will be trimmed down further while still pointing you to the same relevant files. This is a behind-the-scenes adjustment, not something you had to turn on or sign up for.

ai.title: Remove agent name normalization and override types
ai.summary: Deleted `normalizeAgentName` and `normalizeAgentNames` from `common/src/util/agent-name-normalization.ts`, removing implicit stripping of the `CodebuffAI/` org prefix. Removed `common/src/types/agent-overrides.ts` and associated validation logic in `agent-template-validation.ts`. Updated `agent-name-resolver.ts` and `agent-validation.ts` to use raw agent IDs without normalization. Web docs components `AgentOverrideSchemaDisplay` removed from `web/src/components/docs/mdx/`.

eli5.text: When you or your team refers to a built-in agent (like CodebuffAI/claude-code), the system used to quietly strip off the "CodebuffAI/" prefix before looking it up, and also applied hidden rules about which tools or sub-agents were allowed. The system now uses the exact name you type, with no automatic cleanup or override enforcement, so the name you request is the name it tries to load. Users writing agent configuration files in the Codebuff platform won't get silent rewrites of their agent IDs or unexpected rejections based on the old override rules.

ai.title: DynamicAgentTemplateSchema adds tool/outputMode validation rules
ai.summary: Added two refine checks to DynamicAgentTemplateSchema in common/src/types/dynamic-agent-template.ts. First, if 'set_output' is in toolNames, outputMode must be 'json'. Second, if subagents array is non-empty, 'spawn_agents' must be in toolNames. These validations enforce correct tool configuration for JSON output and subagent spawning.

eli5.text: Starting today, the assistant enforces two rules about how it's configured: if it's set to produce JSON output, it must include a specific tool to do so, and if it's given a list of helper agents to spawn, it must include the tool that allows that. You would notice this if you tried to configure the assistant without those required tools, as it would now reject the configuration with a clear message explaining what's missing. These checks live in the shared settings that define valid assistant setups, so any product or feature using those settings will apply them automatically.

eli5.text: The latest version of the Codebuff coding assistant (released August 6, 2025) includes several improvements that users will notice. The assistant's web search feature now works correctly when gathering information, and a new tool has been added to retrieve details about errors that occur during tasks. Additionally, the assistant's file selection and organization capabilities have been streamlined, making it easier for it to understand and work with projects. eli5.text: When you open the CodeBuff command-line tool, it now loads your local agent templates only once at startup instead of loading them again each time it checks project files or connects. If you use the tool, you won't notice any visible change in behavior, but the behind-the-scenes loading process is faster and cleaner. This is a minor housekeeping update that affects only the internal flow of starting up the CLI.

ai.title: Move agent config validation to server
ai.summary: Relaxed client-side Zod schemas in `common/src/types/dynamic-agent-template.ts` and `common/src/util/file.ts` to accept `any` types, shifting strict validation to the server. `npm-app/src/agents/load-agents.ts` removes local `DynamicAgentConfigSchema.parse` calls, storing raw configs with stringified `handleSteps` instead. Error messages in `common/src/templates/agent-validation.ts` now include agent display names and IDs for better context. Covers Core shared types, CLI loader, and validation utilities.

eli5.text: When you load your custom assistants from files, the app now saves the exact content you wrote instead of double-checking every detail on your machine first; the strict checking of names and settings now happens on the remote server that runs the assistants. You might only notice this if your assistant file previously had an unusual or extra setting that the old local check would have rejected before the file was read, those files now load without a local error and are either accepted or flagged by the server with a clearer message that includes your assistant's name and ID. This affects anyone who drops custom assistant files into their project folder, and it is live today.

eli5.text: This is a routine behind-the-scenes update that keeps installs current. It also relaxes some of the checks the program does on agents before they run, moving stricter validation to a remote service instead. If you updated today, you'd experience slightly faster launches and less rigid pre-checks, but no new buttons or features.

eli5.text: The internal assistant setup files got tidied so they no longer carry extra, unused instructions and output rules, which makes those assistants a bit simpler to maintain and keeps their behavior more consistent. If you work with these assistants, you won't see a big shift in what they do day-to-day, but the underlying configuration is cleaner and less cluttered. This cleanup is already in place.

ai.title: Enable middle-out transform for OpenRouter
ai.summary: OpenRouter API integration now includes `transforms: ['middle-out']` in the extra body payload. This change activates middle-out context handling to improve long conversation stability. The update applies to the backend `openrouter.ts` file, affecting all OpenRouter model requests.

eli5.text: Conversations that run through OpenRouter can now stay steadier for longer. The system now tucks a request flag into every OpenRouter-powered conversation so the provider keeps the full back-and-forth intact instead of dropping earlier parts when talks get lengthy. You won't see a button or setting for it; it's already active for anyone whose assistant is routed through OpenRouter, so long chats simply behave more reliably from here on.

ai.title: Print mode accepts APIKEYENVVAR for auth
ai.summary: CLI print mode now checks `process.env[API_KEY_ENV_VAR]` alongside `client.user` to bypass auth errors. Updated error message in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` instructs users to set the env var or run `codebuff login`. Scope limited to CLI entry point. Import `API_KEY_ENV_VAR` from `@codebuff/common/constants`.

eli5.text: When you run CodeBuff in print mode from the command line, it now checks for a special API key stored in your environment settings, not just your logged-in account. This lets automated systems use print mode without needing a full login. If neither the key nor a logged-in account is found, you’ll see a clearer message telling you to either log in or set that API key. This only affects command-line users running in print mode.
